followUp.question: Give an example from automotive or plant engineering where an agent would be the wrong tool, and one where it might be right.
rubric: fixed procedure suits workflow|released work instruction|checklist
open ended diagnosis might suit agent|unknown fault|troubleshooting

transfer.scenario: A product manager asks for 'an agent' that answers 'how many warranty claims did part X get last month' from the claims database.
rubric: single query not an agent|one tool call|text to SQL with validation
exact numbers from the system of record|database query

question: How do you decide between a workflow and an agent, and when would you use neither?

mustCover: workflow when steps are known|fixed steps|predictable path|predefined code paths
agent when steps cant be predicted|open ended|unpredictable path|model chooses the next step
single call when one step is enough|one model call|no agent needed|simple lookup
cost latency and variation|more model calls|compounding errors
start simple and measure|baseline first|evaluate both designs|simplest solution
strongSignals: router sends known intents to workflows
irreversible actions stay coded steps|actions outside the agent
testability and audit|same path every time

followUps.question: What changes if the task moves money or touches customer data?
rubric: coded step for the action|keep the action out of the agent

followUps.question: Give an example where you would pick an agent.
When would you let the agent decide when and what to retrieve, instead of retrieving once before it answers?
rubric: multi hop|vague questions|several searches|search again|follow up searches
search as a tool|search tool|rewrite the query|query rewriting|agentic rag
single shot baseline|fixed retrieval baseline|evaluate both designs|same labelled questions
